newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN TRUTH PROBE SUSPECTS WIDESPREAD BURIALS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN TRUTH PROBE SUSPECTS WIDESPREAD BURIALS.

text.p: South Africa's probe into apartheid crimes said on Thursday agents of the old white-run government appeared to have buried many black guerrillas in unmarked graves to prevent them becoming martyrs for liberation movements.

The Truth and Reconciliation Commission, chaired by Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu, has in recent weeks unearthed the remains of several anti-apartheid activists after tipoffs from former police officers.

"We are looking at leads which show that throughout the country people were buried in a manner which suggests that there was a structured policy of burying people as a way of causing them not to be remembered as heroes," the commission's chief investigator, Dumisa Ntsebezi, told a news conference.

"The manner in which this took place cannot simply have been something which can be attributed to an aberration on the part of the individual policeman," he said, adding that "a substantial" number of activists appeared to have been buried anonymously.
Ntsebezi said the commission was trying to establish if a high-level government directive had been issued on such burials.
He said at least some of those buried had been guerrillas killed in combat, and that the apartheid government would have wanted to prevent them becoming symbols of resistance.
"There was a view that if these persons were handed over to their respective families, there would be commemoration services every year and that would stir up the tide of revolution," Ntsebezi said.
